topic.subject: science
topic.title: Getting to know plants
topic.scope: herbs, shrubs, trees, stem, leaf, root, venation, flower parts, functions of each part

misconceptions.statement: Any small plant with a green stem is a baby tree.
misconceptions.why: Students often assume small size indicates a young stage of a larger organism.
misconceptions.fix: Herbs are a specific category of plants that stay small and have soft, green stems throughout their life.

probe.question: If you see a small plant with a soft green stem, will it definitely grow into a tall tree?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, it is just a baby tree right now.

misconceptions.root_belief: small things are just young versions of big things
misconceptions.source_hint: Rosalind Driver's research on children's ideas

misconceptions.statement: The stem only carries water from the roots to the leaves.
misconceptions.why: Students focus on the upward movement of water and ignore the transport of food.
misconceptions.fix: The stem acts as a two-way street, carrying water/minerals up and food from leaves to other parts.

probe.question: Does the stem carry anything from the leaves to the roots?
probe.wrong_answer: No, it only carries water up from the roots.

misconceptions.root_belief: biological structures have only one function

misconceptions.statement: Plants get their food from the soil through their roots.
misconceptions.why: Everyday experience of 'feeding' plants with fertilizer or water leads to this belief.
misconceptions.fix: Plants make their own food in their leaves using sunlight, air, and water; soil only provides minerals.

probe.question: Where does a plant get the energy-rich food it needs to grow?
probe.wrong_answer: It sucks up food from the soil through roots.

misconceptions.root_belief: all living things eat like humans do

misconceptions.statement: Transpiration is the plant 'sweating' to stay cool like humans.
misconceptions.why: Students apply human physiological experiences to plants.
misconceptions.fix: Transpiration is the loss of water vapor from leaves, which helps in pulling water up from the roots.

probe.question: Why do plants release water vapor from their leaves?
probe.wrong_answer: Because they are hot and need to sweat.

misconceptions.statement: If a plant part is underground, it must be a root.
misconceptions.why: Students use location as the primary defining characteristic rather than structure.
misconceptions.fix: Some stems, like potatoes and ginger, grow underground to store food.

probe.question: Is a potato a root because it grows under the ground?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, everything under the ground is a root.

misconceptions.root_belief: location defines the identity of an object

misconceptions.statement: The green leaf-like parts at the base of a flower are just small leaves.
misconceptions.why: They look identical to leaves in color and texture.
misconceptions.fix: These are sepals, which are specific flower parts that protect the bud.

probe.question: What are the green leaf-like structures protecting a flower bud called?
probe.wrong_answer: They are just baby leaves of the plant.

misconceptions.root_belief: things that look alike are the same thing

misconceptions.statement: All plants have one main thick root going deep into the soil.
misconceptions.why: The taproot is the 'prototypical' root taught first or seen in diagrams.
misconceptions.fix: Many plants, like grass and wheat, have fibrous roots where all roots look similar and spread out.

probe.question: Does a bunch of grass have one main central root?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, every plant has one main thick root.

misconceptions.root_belief: one example represents the whole category

misconceptions.statement: Leaf venation is just a pattern and has no relation to other plant parts.
misconceptions.why: Students see patterns as decorative rather than functional or structural indicators.
misconceptions.fix: Leaf venation is directly linked to the type of root system the plant has.

probe.question: Can you guess the type of roots a plant has by looking at its leaves?
probe.wrong_answer: No, the leaf pattern has nothing to do with the roots.

misconceptions.root_belief: different parts of a system are independent

misconceptions.statement: Only the colorful petals are part of the flower; the inner parts are something else.
misconceptions.why: Petals are the most visible and 'famous' part of the flower.
misconceptions.fix: A flower includes sepals, petals, stamens, and the pistil; all are essential parts.

probe.question: If you remove the petals, is the remaining center part still part of the flower?
probe.wrong_answer: No, the flower is gone once the petals are removed.

misconceptions.root_belief: the most prominent part is the whole object

misconceptions.statement: Sunlight is a material that plants 'eat' to grow.
misconceptions.why: Confusion between energy sources and matter/food.
misconceptions.fix: Sunlight provides the energy for a chemical process; it is not a physical food item.

probe.question: Is sunlight a type of food for the plant?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, it is the main food that plants eat.

misconceptions.root_belief: energy and matter are the same thing

misconceptions.statement: Shrubs are just herbs that have grown for a few years.
misconceptions.why: Difficulty distinguishing between growth stages and distinct biological categories.
misconceptions.fix: Shrubs are a distinct category with hard, woody stems branching near the base, unlike herbs.

probe.question: Will a coriander herb eventually become a rose shrub if we wait long enough?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, it will grow a woody stem and become a shrub.

misconceptions.root_belief: all small plants are just early stages of larger ones

misconceptions.statement: Roots only hold the plant in the ground; they don't do anything else.
misconceptions.why: Anchorage is the most physically obvious function when pulling a weed.
misconceptions.fix: Roots also absorb water and essential minerals from the soil for the plant.

probe.question: If we put a plant in water without soil, why does it need roots?
probe.wrong_answer: It doesn't; roots are only for sticking to the soil.

misconceptions.root_belief: an object has only its most obvious function
